messages.name: records.fetch
messages.content:
--- Personnel Security File Summary ---
Employee ID: 84219
Contractor: EnergyTech Solutions
Position: Systems Engineer (requires a DOE security clearance)
Security Clearance Status: Restricted pending review
QNSP (July 27 2022): Signed statement affirming no illegal drug use; internal audit later revealed cocaine use three times per week from 2020 through August 11 2024.
Treatment History: Entered inpatient alcohol treatment on August 14 2024; failed to report cocaine use as required by DOE Order 472.2A.
Law Enforcement Record: Arrested September 10 2025 for aggravated driving while under the influence after consuming three to five mixed drinks.
Recent Biomarkers: PEth test September 29 2025 returned 152 ng/mL (positive); subsequent tests on October 30, November 25, December 18 2025, and January 14 2026 were negative.
--- End of Summary ---

messages.name: local_security
messages.content: Local Security Office Note (08:30): The LSO has raised substantial doubt regarding the Individual’s eligibility under Guidelines E, G, and H, citing ongoing concerns about substance abuse and incomplete rehabilitation.

messages.name: senior_security_officer
messages.content: We could consider restoring the clearance conditionally, provided the Individual completes an intensive outpatient program.

messages.name: policy_analyst
messages.content: Given the unresolved eligibility concerns, I recommend we deny restoration of the clearance and keep the current restriction in place.

messages.name: policy_doc
messages.content: Memorandum on Clearance Restoration (Section 4.2): The Judge may restore the Individual’s clearance and lift the existing restriction.

messages.name: psych.fetch
messages.content:
--- Psychologist Evaluation Report (Jan 14 2026) ---
Diagnoses: Alcohol Use Disorder, Moderate, Early Remission.
Conclusion: Insufficient evidence of sustained rehabilitation to support clearance restoration.
Self‑Report at Hearing: Individual denied any recent cocaine use.
Evaluator Observation: Noted a pattern of under‑reporting and an overly positive self‑presentation.
Treatment Participation: Multiple alcohol‑treatment programs, AA meetings, and counseling attended; however, no clear, sustained abstinence demonstrated.
--- End of Report ---
